claims.claim: The deepest hole humans have ever dug was finished with a bit narrower than a dinner plate. (A4: a viewer who leaves at second two takes away 'the deepest hole ever is so narrow that its last bit was smaller than a dinner plate'.)
claims.source_checked: Zhu & Huang, Commun. Earth Environ. 7:124 (2026), doi:10.1038/s43247-026-03246-z, PDF from nature.com, p. 2; Lobanov, Chicherov & Sharov, Arktika i Sever 44:267-284 (2021), doi:10.37482/issn2221-2698.2021.44.267, full-text PDF (arcticandnorth.ru/upload/iblock/df4/267_284.pdf), pp. 268, 275, 276 and Fig. 5c; Met Museum API object 201074 (accession 51.86.100)
claims.note: Zhu & Huang (2026): 'remains the deepest vertical borehole ever attempted, reaching 12,262 m'. Lobanov p. 275: 12,262 m 'не превзойдённая до сих пор' (not surpassed to this day). Bit: 'буровой коронкой диаметром 214 мм' (p. 276); Fig. 5c gives the open hole at the bottom as d 215.9 mm. Met 51.86.100 'Dinner plate', diameter 10 1/16 in (25.6 cm). 21.4 cm < 25.6 cm. The hook is true as stated. 'Deepest' means vertical depth: some oil wells are longer in measured length (not checked here) but none is deeper. 'Dug' is loose for 'drilled', but nothing a viewer takes away from it is false. One oddity: the Table 1 row in Zhu & Huang says 'World's deepest vertical well record (1970–1994)', which reads as if the record ended. Their running text says it 'remains' the deepest, and that is what the script uses.

claims.claim: The Soviet Union started drilling it in May 1970, on the Kola Peninsula.
claims.note: 'Бурение было начато 24 мая 1970 г.' (p. 273). Location 'в северо-западной части Кольского полуострова' (p. 272). A USSR Ministry of Geology programme (pp. 270-272).

claims.claim: At the top, the hole was seventy-two centimetres wide. / 72 CM AT THE TOP [28 IN]
claims.where: spoken + on-screen: 72 CM AT THE TOP [28 IN]
claims.source_checked: Lobanov et al. 2021, Fig. 5c 'фактическая конструкция скважины' (p. 276), read from the image embedded in the PDF
claims.note: Fig. 5c: 'd 720 мм / 40 м' marks the outer wall of the top section. 72 cm / 2.54 = 28.3 in, shown as 28 IN.

claims.claim: It was drilled in steps, each narrower than the last, down to a bit just twenty-one centimetres across. / DOWN TO 21 CM [8 IN]; 21 CM BIT [8 IN]
claims.where: spoken + on-screen: DOWN TO 21 CM [8 IN]; 21 CM BIT [8 IN]
claims.source_checked: Lobanov et al. 2021, Fig. 5c and p. 276 text
claims.note: Fig. 5c steps: 720 mm to 40 m, 325 mm to 2,000 m, 245 mm to 8,770 m, then open hole 215.9 mm to 12,262 m. Each is narrower than the one above. Bit 214 mm (p. 276) = 21.4 cm, said as 'twenty-one'. 21.4 cm = 8.43 in, shown as 8 IN. (The 215.9 mm open hole is exactly 8.5 in, but the label is about the bit.)

claims.claim: By 1975, it was over seven kilometres deep. / OVER 7 KM [OVER 4.3 MI]
claims.note: 'Первый этап бурения был завершён в мае 1975 г., когда скважина достигла глубины 7 263 м.' 7 km = 4.35 mi and 7.263 km = 4.51 mi, so 'over 4.3 mi' holds.

claims.claim: In 1979, at almost 9.6 km, it beat the American record. / AMERICAN RECORD
claims.source_checked: Lobanov et al. 2021, p. 274; Zhu & Huang 2026, p. 5 (Bertha Rogers No. 1)
claims.note: 'В июне 1979 г. скважина побила рекорд в 9 583 метра, принадлежащий скважине США, достигнув глубины 9 584 метра.' 9.584 km is 'almost 9.6'. Zhu & Huang name the US well as Bertha Rogers No. 1 (9.58 km, 1974).

claims.claim: By the end of 1983, it had reached twelve kilometres. / 12 KM [7.5 MI]
claims.note: '27 декабря 1983 г. глубина скважины достигла 12 000 м'. 12 km = 7.46 mi, shown as 7.5.

claims.claim: Then, in 1984, the drill string broke, and they had to start again from seven kilometres down. / BACK TO 7 KM [4.4 MI]
claims.where: spoken + on-screen: BACK TO 7 KM [4.4 MI]
claims.note: '27 сентября 1984 г. бурение СГ-3 было продолжено... на глубине более 12 км произошла авария — оборвалась буровая колонна... Лишь спустя 7 месяцев бурение возобновили заново с глубины 7 000 м.' The record branch began at 7,010 m (p. 277). 7.01 km = 4.36 mi, shown as 4.4 MI. A flat 7 km converts to 4.35 mi, which is a rounding knife-edge: acceptable, since the source figure is 7,010 m.

claims.claim: By 1990, the new branch had reached 12,262 metres. / 12,262 M [40,230 FT]
claims.source_checked: Lobanov et al. 2021, pp. 274, 275, 277; Zhu & Huang 2026, p. 2
claims.note: Lobanov p. 275: 'В 1990 г. была достигнута максимальная глубина — 12 262 м'. Lobanov p. 277: the third branch 'начатый на глубине 7 010 м из первого, завершился на 12 262 м'. Zhu & Huang give 1970–1989. 'By 1990' is true on either date. 12,262 m / 0.3048 = 40,229.7 ft, shown as 40,230 FT.

claims.claim: No hole has gone deeper since. / STILL THE DEEPEST
claims.source_checked: Zhu & Huang 2026, p. 2 (received Oct 2025, accepted Jan 2026); Lobanov et al. 2021, pp. 275, 281
claims.note: Zhu & Huang (2026): 'remains the deepest vertical borehole ever attempted' and 'The deepest penetration is the Russia's Kola Superdeep Borehole'. Lobanov: 'не превзойдённая до сих пор' and 'Вот уже 50 лет этот результат остаётся непревзойдённым'. Read as vertical depth, which is what 'deeper' means. The odd '(1970–1994)' in Zhu & Huang's Table 1 is noted under claim 1.

claims.claim: The rock at the bottom was expected to be around 120 degrees. / EXPECTED: 120 °C [248 °F]
claims.note: 'на глубине около 12 км значения температур достигли 212°С, вместо предполагавшихся 120°С'. 120 × 9/5 + 32 = 248 °F. The voice gives no unit; the screen gives °C.

claims.claim: At ten kilometres, it was already 180. / 180 °C AT 10 KM [356 °F AT 6.2 MI]
claims.where: spoken + on-screen: 180 °C AT 10 KM [356 °F AT 6.2 MI]
claims.source_checked: Lobanov et al. 2021, p. 280; Zhu & Huang 2026, p. 2
claims.note: 'реальная температура в скважине на глубине 10 км достигла 180°С' (Lobanov). 'temperatures reached 180 °C at 10 km' (Zhu & Huang). 180 × 9/5 + 32 = 356 °F. 10 / 1.609344 = 6.21 mi.

claims.claim: At the bottom, it was over two hundred. / 212 °C [414 °F]
claims.source_checked: Lobanov et al. 2021, p. 280; Zhu & Huang 2026, p. 2
claims.note: 212 °C at about 12 km in both sources. 212 × 9/5 + 32 = 413.6 °F, shown as 414 °F.

claims.claim: Below seven kilometres, the walls kept caving in, and the hole went oval, with many caverns. / WALLS CAVING IN
claims.note: 'глубже 7 км пошли менее прочные, трещиноватые... породы... ствол принял овальную форму, появилось множество каверн, участились аварии'. 'На глубинах более 7 000 м ствол скважины имел эллипсовидную форму сечения'. In the Archean rocks there were 'обрушениям стенок скважины'. (Lobanov adds that the cavern zones followed tectonic faults; the script does not contradict this.)

claims.claim: Schematic cross-section of the hole, its walls breaking outward into pockets
claims.where: on-screen: caving cross-section (with the 'walls kept caving in ... caverns' line)
claims.source_checked: Lobanov et al. 2021, pp. 277-278; src/shorts/deepest-hole-long/index.tsx (Caving component)
claims.note: What it shows matches the source: the walls collapse outward and caverns form. But the drawing is deliberately not to scale (the code comment says 'Schematic, not to scale'), and neither the screen nor the script says so. A6 requires one of them to. Fix: add a small 'NOT TO SCALE' or 'SCHEMATIC' label to the card.

claims.claim: Drilling stopped in 1992, when its funding was cut. / 1992: FUNDING CUT
claims.source_checked: Lobanov et al. 2021, p. 275; Zhu & Huang 2026, p. 2
claims.note: Lobanov: 'резкое сокращение финансирования не позволило продолжить работы. Бурение прекратили в 1992 г.' Zhu & Huang blame heat instead ('plastic rock flow that repeatedly sealed the hole'). The SOURCES block records this disagreement and why the Russian Academy account was chosen (A3).

claims.claim: The plan had been to go on to thirteen kilometres. / PLAN: 13 KM [8.1 MI]
claims.note: p. 278: in 1992 casing was run 'для продолжения бурения скважины до глубины 13 км'. p. 272: with a design depth of 15 km, the hole was to reach 13 km by 1990. The overall design depth was 15 km (also Zhu & Huang: 'the original goal was 15 km'). In context, the line is about the 1992 continuation, so 13 km is right. 13 km = 8.08 mi, shown as 8.1.

claims.claim: It never made it through the crust: it got about a third of the way. / STILL IN THE CRUST
claims.where: spoken + on-screen: STILL IN THE CRUST
claims.source_checked: Clarke et al., USGS Open-File Report 86-517 (1986), pubs.usgs.gov/of/1986/0517/report.pdf, summary and 'Results of deep geophysical studies'
claims.note: 'Crustal thickness in the vicinity of the corehole was shown to be about 40 km' (USGS). The same report gives the average Moho depth on the Kola Peninsula as 37 km (range 28-40). 12.262 / 40 = 0.31 and 12.262 / 37 = 0.33, so 'about a third'. Zhu & Huang also say it did not reach the Moho.

claims.claim: Twelve kilometres down. The centre of the Earth is over six thousand more. / 12 KM DOWN [7.5 MI]; 6,000+ KM MORE [3,700+ MI]
claims.where: spoken + on-screen: 12 KM DOWN [7.5 MI]; 6,000+ KM MORE [3,700+ MI]
claims.note: Volumetric mean radius 6,371.000 km; polar radius 6,356.752 km. 6,371 − 12.262 = 6,358.7 km, and even the polar radius leaves 6,344 km, so 'over six thousand'. 6,000 km = 3,728 mi, so '3,700+' holds. 12 km = 7.46 mi, shown as 7.5.

claims.claim: Dinner-plate photo (25.6 cm across) with circles of 21 cm and 72 cm drawn to the same scale
claims.source_checked: Met Museum API objects/201074: accession 51.86.100, 'Dinner plate', diameter 25.6 cm, additionalImages includes 150793.jpg; src/shorts/deepest-hole-long/index.tsx (PLATE_CM = 25.6); Lobanov Fig. 5c
claims.note: The plate photographed is Met 51.86.100 (image 150793 belongs to object 201074), 25.6 cm by the museum's record. The circles are scaled from PLATE_CM. 21 cm is the 214 mm bit rounded; 72 cm is the 720 mm top section.

claims.claim: Depth chart, scales: 0 / 5 / 10 KM on the left; 2 / 4 / 6 / 8 MI on the right; years 1970 / 1980 / 1990
claims.note: The mile ticks sit at 3.22, 6.44, 9.66 and 12.87 km on the same linear scale as the km ticks, which is correct.

claims.claim: Chart dots: (1970.39, 0), (1975.37, 7.263 km), (1979.45, 9.584 km), (1983.99, 12.0 km), joined by dashed lines; dashed 'US RECORD' line at 9.583 km
claims.note: 24 May 1970 = 1970.39. May 1975 / 7,263 m: 1975.37 falls in May. June 1979 / 9,584 m: 1979.45 falls in June. 27 Dec 1983 / 12,000 m = 1983.99. The US record is 9,583 m. The dashes only join readings and claim no depths between them; the ~1-year rig change in 1975-76 is not drawn, which the dashed convention allows.

claims.claim: Chart: dashed line on to (1984.74, 12.066 km), then a solid line back up to (1984.74, 7.01 km)
claims.note: 27 Sep 1984 = 1984.74. The broken branch ended at 12,066 m and the record branch began at 7,010 m (p. 277). Lobanov is internally loose on when 12,066 m was reached: p. 274 says 1983, while p. 277 has a further 9 m drilled on the 27 Sep 1984 run. The difference is about 4 px on this scale, and the dashed segment does not claim intermediate depths.

claims.claim: Chart: dashed line from (1984.74, 7.01 km) to a bar at 12,262 m spanning 1989 to 1990
claims.source_checked: Lobanov et al. 2021, pp. 274, 275, 277; Zhu & Huang 2026, p. 2; src/shorts/deepest-hole-long/index.tsx (bar drawn X(1989) to X(1990))
claims.note: The bar is meant to cover both readings: 1989 (Zhu & Huang) and 1990 (Lobanov, 'В 1990 г. была достигнута максимальная глубина — 12 262 м'; also 12,262 m 'по состоянию на 01.05.1991'). But it is drawn from 1 Jan 1989 to 1 Jan 1990, so it covers none of 1990, the year the cited Russian Academy source gives. Fix: run the bar to the end of 1990 (X(1991)), or start-of-1989 to end-of-1990. A smaller point: Lobanov p. 277 says drilling restarted from 7 km only 'спустя 7 месяцев' (~spring 1985). Starting the dashed branch at ~1985.3 instead of 1984.74 would match that; it is about 17 px on the chart.

claims.claim: Chart: dashed horizontal line at 13 km labelled 'PLAN'
claims.note: 13 km: the target for 1990 (p. 272) and for the 1992 continuation (p. 278). See claim 17 for the 15 km design depth.

claims.claim: Thermometer: °C scale 0/50/100/150/200 with °F 32/122/212/302/392 against the same marks; dashed mark at 120 °C; mercury rising to 180 then 212 °C
claims.note: °F = °C × 9/5 + 32 gives 32, 122, 212, 302, 392, all correct. The 120 / 180 / 212 °C marks match the source (claims 11-13).

claims.claim: Cross-section of crust over mantle with the hole drawn one third of the way down the crust
claims.note: 12.262 / ~40 km = 0.31 (0.33 for a 37 km Moho), so a third is within 'about'. The scaled quantity, depth as a fraction of crustal thickness, is drawn correctly.
